Coming from Python

Source: vignettes/articles/python.Rmd
python.Rmd

This package is a port of the core of the Python package nglscenes. The concepts are the same but the API follows R conventions.

The main differences

  • Copy-on-modify: Python modifies scenes and layers in place (scene.add_layers(layer)), R returns modified copies (sc <- ngs_add_layers(sc, layer)).
  • Functions instead of methods: methods become ngs_-prefixed functions that take the scene or layer as first argument.
  • 1-based indexing: layers are referred to by name or by position starting at 1. Negative indices are not supported.
  • Segment IDs are character vectors, because R can’t represent 64-bit integers exactly as numbers.
  • Not ported: LocalScene (live sync with a local neuroglancer server), local mesh/skeleton layers and the local data server.

Editing layers inside a scene

In Python, scene.layers["seg"] returns the layer object itself, so editing it edits the scene. In R you either use the replacement form of ngs_layer():

library(nglscenes)
sc <- ngs_scene(ngs_segmentation_layer("precomputed://gs://x/seg", name = "seg"))
ngs_layer(sc, "seg")$selectedAlpha <- 0.3

or pass the scene to the helpers, picking the layer with layer:

sc <- ngs_add_segments(sc, c("1", "2"), layer = "seg")
sc <- ngs_set_colors(sc, "red", layer = "seg")

Same JSON

Both packages write keys in sorted order and use the shortest number representations, so the same scene gives the same JSON (and URL) in R and Python.
